pr.title: Align local dependency setup and commit hooks
pr.body:
Align local dependency setup and commit-hook behavior with the selected shared tooling contracts. Python-backed hooks use a hashed requirements closure and an isolated Python 3.12 launcher. Ubuntu contributors first create and activate a Python 3.12 virtual environment, avoiding missing pip and externally managed system installations; the environment is excluded from Git. Normal locked setup installs Husky unless `HUSKY=0` is explicit. Commit hooks check staged Markdown, then all outer and nested Markdown content.

The maintenance classifier now recognizes the launcher, requirements and related validation helpers, so standalone changes receive the intended maintenance checks. Retained behavioral tests exercise the actual launcher with bounded external interpreter probes: unapproved modules, exact-version and missing-runtime failures, `-E -P` dispatch, forwarded arguments and native exit status. The probe tests do not attest installed Python packages or simulate Python's isolation effects; separate real Python controls cover their stated behavior.

Keep the accepted npm graph and runtime pins. The audit helper and tests share one reviewed repository-identity constant, package metadata is aligned, and contributor instructions describe the actual commands. This twenty-file change preserves the existing workflows, protected instructions and validator API.

Review dispositions:

- Maintenance classification reuses the independently reviewed complete six-selector closure and its tests, preserving the classifier algorithm and accepted caller regression.
- Linux setup uses the native venv facility and one `.venv/` exclusion. The canonical isolated/hash/binary/explicit-index installation command and Windows setup remain unchanged. The selected solution avoids system-package overrides and a new bootstrap framework.
- Launcher regression coverage belongs in the existing CI-helper suite. All existing tests remain, including the missing-runner-variable failure-before-external-work check, whose diagnostic assertion is aligned with the selected common wording.

The [finding decisions](https://github.com/franklesniak/PSStyleGuide/blob/8a2df213f534cf9fcb064071912a38eab09b3b4c/docs/planning/action-items-2026-10-02/results/A07/review-r1-decisions.md) preserve the alternatives, evidence and limits behind these choices; this body records their product-facing disposition.

Validation for commit `c9e0b24cd3b4ea8aef87a954f5f67e7b6ce0a6f8`:

- The complete existing five-file Node caller passes: Linux 201/201; Windows 115 passed and 86 existing Linux-only skips. All four new launcher tests run on both platforms. Six deliberately unsafe launcher variants fail their intended test on each platform.
- Actual Ubuntu 24.04/Python 3.12.3 controls reproduce missing pip and externally managed installation failures, then pass the documented venv/hash-locked installation, pip check and real launcher success/failure cases. Git controls verify `.venv/` is excluded while authored and modified tracked files remain selectable.
- One full all-files pre-commit run passes all 11 hooks, including the full instruction SelfTest; all 75 frozen raw/index entries remain unchanged. Normal commit hooks pass. Actual accepted-base `2a2d14a` / candidate `c9e0b24` metadata finalization, classification and proposed-policy checks pass.
- A fresh ordinary audit of both installed roots is CLEAN, with no findings or risk exceptions, using normally refreshed native-main authority `2a2d14a`. Its offline authority/freshness limitation remains explicit.
- Independent source and repair review found no actionable findings. Earlier actual Windows/Linux hook, locked-installation and Markdown failure-propagation evidence remains applicable to the unchanged implementation; the repaired candidate also passes the complete caller above.

The separate paired-repository task still requires the Terraform counterpart and reverse comparison. Candidate and landed CI remain distinct acceptance gates. This is the remaining tooling batch after accepted PR #225.
